correctness.rationale: Quadratic residues mod17 give the eight-regular undirected Paley graph with 17 vertices, 68 edges, 68 triangles, and no four-cliques. An independent graph enumeration reproduces these exact counts. The provided 16-edge spanning tree was independently checked connected, and every one of the 52 specified triangular relators has exactly one still-unknown non-tree edge in the given order, exhausting all 52 edge generators. This kills π1 and yields a 52-by-52 unit triangular boundary minor. With no cells above dimension two, ∂2 rank52 and integral H2 is free rank68−52=16; simply connected Hurewicz and Whitehead give wedge_16 S². Independent signed Lefschetz enumeration across all 136 affine transformations x↦ax+b (a a quadratic residue) gives character frequencies identity 1 with 16, 16 nontrivial translations with −1, 119 nontranslations with 0. This matches the vertex permutation module with its invariant line removed. Character equality identifies the rational G-module by semisimplicity; no integral equivariant lattice isomorphism is asserted. The fixed-sign contribution for a=−1 correctly includes both fixed edges and triangles.

value.rationale: The small canonical self-complementary conference graph P17 is a natural test object in flag-complex topology. The theorem supplies both complete integral homotopy classification and a full nontrivial 136-element group representation, information not captured by graph spectra, Euler characteristic or neighborhood-complex topology. The fixed-face parity calculation identifies a distinctive canonical augmentation module and is a motivated finite classification rather than arbitrary parameter slicing.

final_claim: The Paley17 clique complex has integral homotopy type wedge of 16 S² and its natural 136-element affine group acts on rational H2 as the 16-dimensional vertex augmentation representation; trace 16 on identity, -1 on nontrivial translations and 0 otherwise.
limitations: No extension of the wedge theorem to other Paley field sizes.
Character comparison is over Q, not an integral equivariant lattice isomorphism.
